newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan says earnings hurt by lower aluminum prices.
newsitem.headline: Alcan says earnings hurt by lower aluminum prices.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd. Thursday reported earnings of nearly $100 million for the latest quarter but the giant aluminum producer said its results were still hurt by a drop in metal prices.

The company said it earned $97 million, or 43 cents a share, in the third quarter on revenues of $1.9 billion vs. a loss of $142 million, or 63 cents a share, on revenues of $2.2 billion a year-ago when it wrote down its investment in a hydroelectric project.
The results also compared with second-quarter earnings of $107 million, or 47 cents a share, on revenues of $1.97 billion.
"Further customer destocking in the U.S., seasonal slowing in Europe and increased competition in export markets led volumes to slip from second quarter levels," said Chief Executive Jacques Bougie.
"This, together with the fallout from substantially lower primary prices, had an adverse impact on profitability."
Aluminum prices hovered Thursday at a 2-1/2-year low of $1,305 a metric ton on the London Metal Exchange, depressed by over-supply and slack consumer demand.
Bougie said Alcan sees a stable outlook in North America and improving conditions in Europe.
"On a positive note, we are now seeing some early signs of improvement in Europe and business conditions in North America remain stable, particularly in the non-can sheet sectors," Bougie said.
In last year's third quarter, Alcan wrote-down its $420 million investment in the hydroelectric Kemano Completion Project in British Columbia.
